title: Feed a captive nut under channel lips
context: A fastener in an enclosed channel must enter through the open end. Its wide head must finish under both retaining lips. This tests a constrained assembly path while the other arm braces the loose channel.
scoring: Score zero if the channel centre ever moves more than 5 mm from its starting position or if the nut goes more than 5 mm below the table. The nut must pass the front entry gate with x within 5 mm of 260 mm and y between negative 85 mm and negative 55 mm and its lower face within 6 mm of z 757.5 mm. This earns 0.25. After entry a nut x within 6 mm of 260 mm and y between negative 20 mm and 66 mm with its upper face below z 812.5 mm earns 0.5. A seated nut must have x within 4 mm of 260 mm and y within 5 mm of 60 mm and its lower face within 4 mm of z 757.5 mm. Tilt and yaw must be below 5 degrees. It must move below 8 mm per second and 0.1 radians per second. This earns 0.75. Both measured grippers open beyond 35 mm raises this to 1.0. Full success must hold for 2 seconds. All other outcomes score zero.
fidelity: The channel and nut are rigid printed polymer solids. The broad nut head physically fits below both rigid lips. There is no threaded engagement or screw tightening. The long nut handle gives the gripper access above the lips. Contacts use PhysX defaults with a 1 mm contact offset. No elastic material deformation is simulated.
instruction: Hold the grey channel still. Feed the blue T nut through its open front end and slide it to the white end mark. The wide head must be below both retaining lips. Release both grippers. Keep the channel within 5 mm of its starting position. All equipment is unpowered.
setup: Use the bimanual YAM station with the tabletop at z 747.5 mm. x points forward. y points left. z points up. Every part is printed PA12 polymer. scene_inventory.json lists every object and every solid with exact dimensions and initial positions in metres and masses in kilograms. Object positions use the world frame. Solid positions use their body frame. Joint anchors and limits are listed with the articulated object. The setup image shows this fixed layout. All joint positions start at zero.
run_limit: 600 control steps at 20 Hz. This is 30 seconds of control time.
reset_notes: Restore every object to the starting pose in scene_inventory.json and every joint to zero. Nothing is consumed. Use one epoch with seed 0 and object_jitter=0.
scores: Both uploaded videos show the same scripted demo with score 1.0. No model score is claimed.
